$comment: Variant module: CHRONOLOGY. Byline: Claude Code · Opus 5 · 2026-08-29 12:59 EDT. Self-contained per the modularity rule. Parent registry: ../document-markdown-v1.json. This is the only variant that emits a timeline artifact.

detect.$comment: Thresholds derived from ONE measured instance. Starting point, not a calibrated classifier.

pass_chunk.$comment: FULL coverage. Runs independently of artifact extraction — nothing is carved out.
pass_chunk.never_split: a single dated entry — its date and narrative must stay in one chunk
pass_chunk.heading_note: The document's level-3 headings are era/section labels (e.g. 'PART I — MASTER CHRONOLOGY'). Carry the enclosing heading as chunk context so an entry is interpretable standalone.
pass_chunk.rationale: Register R58 — the pattern IS the evidence. Splitting a dated entry destroys the unit a chronology exhibit cites.
pass_chunk.coverage_requirement: Non-entry text (headings, preamble, interstitial prose) must still land in chunks. The completeness gate in the parent registry applies unchanged.

pass_artifact.$comment: SEPARATE pass. Owner ruling 2026-08-29: extraction happens separately from chunking — everything still goes into chunks, AND this artifact is also produced. Re-derivable without re-chunking.
pass_artifact.runs: in parallel with pass_chunk, over the same source
pass_artifact.consumes: the source document — NOT the chunks

target_contract.$comment: Column mapping onto the live table. Authority: sql/0035_timeline_projection.sql:62-95. UNIQUE (source_system, source_record_id, source_record_version) — that triple is the idempotency key.

source_system.note: The table's own comment lists 'ai_chat' as an expected source_system, and D-082 records that an AI-chat-derived row is a LEAD, never evidence.

source_record_id.derive: stable id for the entry — recommend sha256(source_sha256 + ':' + char_start)
source_record_id.note: must be stable across re-runs or idempotency breaks

source_record_version.note: lets a re-extraction under a new schema coexist rather than collide

source_locator.note: Bounded pointer for source-opening (R33). char offsets come from the SAME primitive the chunker emits, so an artifact row joins to its chunk by range overlap.

extraction_run_id.note: table takes free text — no FK required (WP-B01 typed run table not yet built)

temporal_precision.note: NOT NULL. See date_form_mapping — the table comment is explicit: never coerce imprecision into a false-precision point.

display_summary.derive: the entry's narrative text, verbatim where possible

event_type.note: NOT NULL, controlled vocabulary versioned at the projection layer, not enforced by the table

entity_refs.note: person/place references found in the entry

date_form_mapping.$comment: Measured against the real entries in the reference instance, not hypothesised. Owner ruling 2026-08-29: 'if all you have is a rough reference or rough date or a span, input that as a separate field without an exact timestamp.' Imprecise placement is NOT this extractor's job to resolve — a separate relative-date engine owns that and is a work in progress.

tiers.note: A span with no single timestamp is directly expressible today — occurred_at stays NULL.

tiers.hard_rule: Bound it only to the granularity the source actually states. 'Summer 2023' bounds to that season — it does NOT become a day.

tiers.action: DEFER to the relative-date subsystem. Emit no timestamps at all.
tiers.note: This is the case the separate engine exists for. Do not guess bounds to make the row look complete.

date_form_mapping.hard_rule: NEVER fabricate a timestamp to satisfy a column. An absent date is a fact about the source; an invented one is a defect that becomes evidence.

preserve_raw.rule: In every tier, carry the source's date phrase VERBATIM alongside the parsed values.
preserve_raw.why: The phrase is the primary record; the parse is a derived interpretation. A reviewer must be able to see 'Summer 2023' and judge the bounding for themselves. This is also what lets the relative-date engine re-derive placement later without re-reading the document.

relative_date_handoff.$comment: VERIFIED 2026-08-29 13:0x against sql/0047_content_chunk_and_context_thread_foundation.sql. Owner: a separate engine for placing events without exact dates is a work in progress and will evolve; a table already exists.
relative_date_handoff.status_of_target: UNTRACKED / IN-FLIGHT — sql/0047 is not committed as of this writing. Treat its shape as volatile and re-verify before implementing.

shape_observed.review: review_state IN (proposed, approved, rejected, superseded); approved requires reviewed_by + reviewed_at
shape_observed.versioning: anchor_key + version_ordinal, supersedes_id — corrections are new versions, not edits
shape_observed.at_least_one_required: CHECK enforces at least one of lower_bound / upper_bound / before-anchor / after-anchor / sequence_key

relative_date_handoff.design_intent_quoted: Its own header comment: 'Primary tables retain their authoritative occurred_at/acquisition clocks. These versioned assertions express only an unresolved or approximate placement when a primary clock is unavailable.' That is exactly the split this variant follows — precise placement on the primary row, imprecise placement as a separate anchor.

GAP.finding: There is NO link table between timeline.event_candidate and context.relative_time_anchor. Verified: zero matches in sql/0047. The relative-time subsystem currently links to THREAD entities only — first/third_party_thread_version, _source, and _message anchors.
GAP.consequence: A chronology entry whose date is unbounded/relative has nowhere to record its anchor today. It can only be emitted as temporal_precision='uncertain' with all timestamps NULL and the raw phrase preserved.
GAP.recommended: An event_candidate ↔ relative_time_anchor link table, following the same typed-link pattern 0047 already uses (its comment: 'Typed link tables prevent weak entity_type/entity_id pointers or nullable-FK soup'). Do NOT add a nullable anchor_id column to event_candidate — that is the pattern 0047 explicitly rejects.
GAP.owner_note: Flagged, not built. The engine is WIP and will evolve; this schema should follow it rather than pre-empt it.

pass_artifact.authority_note: Rows are CANDIDATE authority only (D-082 — an AI-chat-derived row is a lead, never evidence). The table is append-only via timeline.forbid_mutation(); a correction is a NEW row with a new extraction_run_id, never an edit.
pass_artifact.downstream: timeline.timeline_member with member_authority='candidate_context' → timeline projection/generation (server/timeline/, currently CLI-only with zero production callers).

known_content_hazards.$comment: Measured in the reference instance — flag so an extractor does not silently mangle them.
known_content_hazards.escaped_markdown: Headings contain escaped ordinals (e.g. '**PART I — MASTER CHRONOLOGY**'); entries use '> * **' prefixes. Treat the '\.' escapes as source text, not markup.
known_content_hazards.name_variants: The source itself records name reconciliations (a legal name vs a phonetic spelling; an actor known by a short form). Entity extraction MUST NOT silently normalise these — R17 identity resolution is a reviewed step, and the document is evidence of the variance itself.
known_content_hazards.em_dash_ranges: Date ranges use en/em dashes, not hyphens. A hyphen-only range regex will miss them.

open_questions: source_record_id derivation is a recommendation, not a decision — it must be stable across re-runs, and the choice affects the UNIQUE idempotency triple.
event_type controlled vocabulary is undefined for this variant. The table does not enforce it; the projection layer versions it.

Whether extraction is deterministic (rule-based on date forms) or model-assisted. If model-assisted, the determinism guard applies: the model proposes a schema/mapping once, a deterministic pass applies it, and the result is pinned by schema_version.
